body.p: Claims 1, 14-17 and 19 are AMENDED. Support for the amendments may be found at least at para [0066] to [0070] of the Specification, as originally filed. Thus, claims 1-19 remain pending.

Applicant would like to thank the Examiner for indicating allowable subject matter in the Specification at eqns 1(a)-1(d). Applicant submits that independent claims 1, 14, and 19 are amended to incorporate the allowable subject matter regarding the nominal control law solving an optimization problem.

Applicant submits that the alleged combination of prior arts fails to teach or suggest the features of "A controller for controlling a motion of a spacecraft in a multi-object celestial system while avoiding an unauthorized entry into a keep-away zone during a normal and an abnormal operation of the spacecraft ... execute, during the normal operation of the spacecraft, a nominal control law subject to constraints on maintaining a state of the spacecraft within a union of a plurality of control invariant sets of values of the state of the spacecraft that partially or completely enclose the keep-away zone ", as recited in amended independent claim 1.

Cited art '724 publication is directed towards an Unmanned plane 310 having an inertial measurement unit for obtaining inertial guidance data that includes amongst other things flying height information and airspeed information. Applicant submits that the '724 publication is not directed towards spacecrafts operating in a multi-object celestial system; instead, it is applicable to aircrafts that operate within the Earth's atmosphere. The physics of dynamics and forces applicable in a multi-object celestial system is entirely different from that of an aircraft which operates within the Earth's atmosphere. Accordingly, the teachings of '724 publication cannot lead one of ordinary skill the art towards the claimed controller for controlling a motion of a spacecraft in a multi-object celestial system.
Furthermore, '724 publication does not teach or suggest the feature "constraints on maintaining a state of the spacecraft within a union of a plurality of control invariant sets of values
of the state of the spacecraft that partially or completely enclose the keep-away zone" as recited in amended claim 1. The Office Action relied on Chen to conclude that said feature is obvious.

Chen describes a satellite anomaly detection system that obtains satellite telemetry data and determines whether the satellite performs normal operation or abnormal operation based on a Mahalanobis distance. Applicant submits that while Chen describes categorization of the satellite's operation, it does not teach or suggest executing a nominal control law subject to constraints on maintaining a state of the spacecraft within a union of a plurality of control invariant sets of values of the state of the spacecraft that partially or completely enclose the keep-away zone.

In fact, neither Chen nor the '724 publication discloses anything regarding such constraints on maintaining a state of the spacecraft within sets of states of the spacecraft that partially or completely enclose the keep-away zone. The learned Examiner is providing bits and pieces mapping of the claimed invention with the prior arts without considering the essence of the claimed features. Applicant submits that such cherry picking of teachings of the prior arts is impermissible within the ambit of 35 U.S.C. 103.

Furthermore, at the time of the claimed invention, it would not have been obvious for one of ordinary skill in the art to have combined the teachings of Chen with those of the '724 publication because the two are from different domains. Particularly, extending the principles of aircrafts to spacecrafts is not ordinary skill in the art because of differences in the physics of the dynamics of the two vehicles.
Berning and Goo cited for other reasons fails to remedy the deficiencies of '724 publication and Chen.

For these reasons, Applicant submits that the prior arts of record are not relevant to the claimed invention and the Examiner is respectfully requested to reconsider the rejection of independent claim 1.
Independent claim 14 and 19 also recites analogous features with respect to claim 1 and are therefore also allowable at least for the same reasons as presented above for independent claim
Dependent claims 2-13 and 15-18 are also allowable at least due to their dependence on independent claim 1 or 14.
Reconsideration and allowance of claims 1-19 is respectfully requested.

Applicant respectfully submits that pending claims 1-19 are in condition for allowance, and respectfully requests an early and favorable action by the Examiner. If the Examiner believes that a telephone conversation with Applicant's agent would expedite prosecution of this application, the Examiner is cordially invited to call the undersigned attorney of record.
